definitions.explanation: the board used to play shogi (Japanese chess), traditionally a thick wooden block with a 9x9 grid

examples.japanese: {将棋盤|しょうぎばん}に{駒|こま}を{並|なら}べる。
examples.english: To line up the pieces on the shogi board.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}から{古|ふる}い{将棋盤|しょうぎばん}をもらった。
examples.english: I received an old shogi board from my grandfather.

examples.japanese: {高級|こうきゅう}な{将棋盤|しょうぎばん}は{榧|かや}の{木|き}で{作|つく}られ、{脚|あし}{付|つ}きで{数十万円|すうじゅうまんえん}するものもある。
examples.english: High-quality shogi boards are made from kaya wood, and leg-mounted ones can cost hundreds of thousands of yen.

notes:
The board used for {将棋|しょうぎ} (Japanese chess). Composed of {将棋|しょうぎ} (shogi) + {盤|ばん} (board). A standard {将棋盤|しょうぎばん} has a 9x9 grid of 81 squares. Professional and formal boards are thick blocks of wood, often made from {榧|かや} (Japanese torreya), and stand on four legs.

TYPES:
- {脚|あし}{付|つ}き{将棋盤|しょうぎばん} — leg-mounted shogi board (formal, sits on the floor)
- {卓上|たくじょう}{将棋盤|しょうぎばん} — tabletop shogi board (thinner, placed on a table)
- {折|お}り{畳|たた}み{将棋盤|しょうぎばん} — folding shogi board (portable, casual play)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {将棋盤|しょうぎばん}に{向|む}かう — to sit down at the shogi board
- {将棋盤|しょうぎばん}と{駒|こま} — shogi board and pieces
- {将棋盤|しょうぎばん}を{挟|はさ}んで — across the shogi board (facing each other)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {碁盤|ごばん} — go board (19x19 grid for the game of go)
- {盤面|ばんめん} — board position/state (the current arrangement of pieces)
- チェス{盤|ばん} — chess board
